summary: Implement Phase 2: universal Git message validation and hook installation

decisions.problem: Shell substring parsing cannot validate Git commits; a universal commit-msg hook validator is needed to check actual message files and staged records.
decisions.choice: Implement check-message CLI parsing trailers with git interpret-trailers, inspecting the staged record from index, validating schema and code manifest digest, with advisory warning and strict rejection modes.
decisions.rationale: Validating the actual Git message file and inspecting the staged record directly from the index covers all commit workflows (-m, -F, amend, editors) reliably.

decisions.problem: Hook installation must not overwrite foreign hook managers or global configurations, and must execute across varying agent and GUI PATHs on Windows and POSIX.
decisions.choice: Implement hook install and uninstall CLI with core.hooksPath resolution, global config safety, marked idempotent launcher with Python fallbacks, and foreign hook preservation.
decisions.rationale: Marked blocks and executable fallback chains guarantee idempotency, safe coexistence, and cross-platform portability.

decisions.problem: Integration tests and documentation are required to verify the complete commit-msg hook lifecycle, strict/advisory modes, amend/merge/empty policies, and foreign hook preservation across platforms.
decisions.choice: Implement 29 comprehensive test cases in tests/integration/test_hooks.py and document check-message and hook commands in README.md and CAPABILITY_LEDGER.md.
decisions.rationale: End-to-end Git commit subprocess execution proves that strict mode leaves HEAD unchanged upon failure and permits commits upon success without regression.
